item.title: Race as a construct: busting medical myths with Dr. Joel Bervell
item.description:
Dr. Joel Bervell is an award winning trailblazer in clinical science communication. In addition to his practice he has built a science communication channel focusing on racial disparities in clinical care. Here he analyses two twins that could be considered different races despite being siblings from the same parents.
Responding to race as a social construct. Social construct does not mean imaginary. Race impacts are very real. When we think of skincare, hair care, economic conditions, treatment by police, we see clear delineations of racial impacts.
The history of the construction of race is wild to dive into. Standard repost disclosures: I am NOT Joel Bervell, he is found on yt, ig, tt, @joelbervell to follow, support, and engage with

item.title: Mapquest thanks google for shooting themselves in the foot.
item.description: MapQuest’s mobile app has consequently surged in popularity, rising its way to becoming the number one navigation app in all of the US on Apple’s App Store. It’s become so popular, in fact, that it also climbed to the fourth position on the App Store’s Top Charts, which excludes games, and number eight overall across apps and games. "We’re not changing it,” MapQuest declared in the viral post with a screenshot of a map showing Lake Ontario. Clearly relishing the moment, MapQuest made another dig days later. “We are aware that Lake Ontario is being correctly labeled on our map,” it posted. https://futurism.com/artificial-intelligence/google-maps-rival-surges-lake-ontario

item.title: Victory!!
item.description: In 2020, just 5 months after my father passed away, I was diagnosed with breast cancer. I didn’t know if I had enough strength to fight this battle, but with the loving support of my family and friends, I got through it, and today I got to the milestone of being 5yrs cancer free! I am so thankful to everyone who helped me, including the doctors and nurses, so, thank you to all of them! Also, thanks to all of you here on imjur, who sent me well wishes & encouragement at the beginning of this journey! To those of you out there who are still battling any kind of cancer, you are in my thoughts, and I wish you a full & speedy recovery. Never underestimate your ability to fight this battle. You are stronger than you think!

item.title: GovBrief Today #577
item.description: Donald Trump asked the FCC to punish a journalist for doubting him. Kristen Welker reported on NBC that his primary endorsement record was mixed. Six of his candidates lost Republican primaries in August. Trump called her a "Hostess," accused her of "purposeful inaccuracy," and said she would be reported to the FCC "for rebuke or punishment." In June she interviewed him in a Wisconsin barn and asked for evidence of his claim that California was rigging its primary count. He told her "you're either crooked or you're stupid," said he'd had enough, and walked out with "Thank you, darling." He handled that one himself. Now he wants FCC Chair Brendan Carr to handle it for him. I've emailed 8,882 stories over 577 straight nights, free and without ads. The algorithm can't show them all to you.
